messages:

Subject: Proposal: 3-year price shelter for Redwood services

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Leadership at OptiMed is comfortable moving from pilot to platform-wide usage, but they need price certainty as they budget multi-year projects. They asked whether Redwood can provide a 36-month price shelter (cap on annual uplift at 5% and a renewal protection clause guaranteeing no surprise-wide re-pricing for in-contract accounts).

Attached is a high-level usage projection and a short note from our CFO. Can you confirm whether you have levers to offer that kind of protection and, if so, what approvals are required? They have an internal procurement deadline on 2028-03-20.

Best,
Jordan Hayes
VP IT Strategy, OptiMed
OptiMed Inc.
Attachments: OptiMed_usage_summary.pdf, OptiMed_CFO_note.pdf

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-11T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Proposal: 3-year price shelter for Redwood services

Forwarding OptiMed request - they want a 36-month price shelter: uplift capped at 5%/yr and formal renewal protection (no account-wide re-pricing mid-term; standard exceptions for extraordinary legislation). OptiMed is ramping from 5k to ~40k tokens/month in year 1 and expects 3x growth yr-over-yr.

Ask: Executive approval for non-standard multi-year price protection + authority to offer a conditional 12-month invoice credit if we miss SLOs in yr1. I am proposing: 1) list price discount schedule in attached price-modeling-3yr.xlsx (volume thresholds), 2) cap uplift at 5%/yr, 3) renewal protection clause limited to commercial-rate changes (no technical compatibility clauses), 4) finance holdback of 8% in year 1 as a SLO buffer.

Need decision and any alternate guardrails by COB 2028-03-14 to meet OptiMed procurement timeline.

--
Lauren Bishop
Sr. Director, Strategic Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
Attachments: OptiMed_MA_plan_v3.pdf, price-modeling-3yr.xlsx, renewal-safeguard-draft.docx

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai; markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-11T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Proposal: 3-year price shelter for Redwood services

Lauren — thanks for the clear ask and the math. A couple of redlines and clarifying questions from my side: 

- Renewal protection: we can offer protection against list price inflation for customer-facing rates, but we need a carve-out for capacity-driven surcharge (e.g., sudden GPU market shocks). Proposal: anchor to CPI + explicit maximum (5% as requested) and a carve-out for force majeure/cost-pass events with 30 days' notice.
- Holdback: I am uneasy about a finance holdback that reduces cashflow for a net-new enterprise; if used, it should be an escrow that releases on quarterly SLO checks rather than an 8% unilateral deduction.
- Multi-year discount: need sign-off from Finance on modeled gross margin at 3yr volume; Marissa, can you run a 3-yr margin sensitivity and confirm worst-case margin at the proposed thresholds?

If Finance signs off, I will approve up to 20% aggregate discount across the term provided the renewal protection language includes the carve-outs above and an opt-out if we hit sustained >40% usage above forecast (we should add a consumption-triggered repricing clause).

Ben
VP, Sales Strategy
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai; ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-11T15:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Proposal: 3-year price shelter for Redwood services

I ran the sensitivity on the attached price-modeling-3yr.xlsx. Key takeaways:

- Base case (forecast usage): gross margin remains >55% if uplift capped at 5% and discounts limited to the schedule in sheet 'Tiers'.
- Downside (40% higher consumption than forecast): margin compresses to ~28% in year 2; that's below our comfort threshold for a multi-year committed structure.
- Suggested guardrails: a quarterly reconciliation with a consumption-tier true-up, and an express repricing trigger if average monthly consumption exceeds forecast by 35% for two consecutive quarters.

I can sign off on up to 18% aggregate discount if legal adds the quarterly true-up and consumption-trigger repricing. Also recommend replacing the cash holdback with an SLO credit up to 4% per quarter (caps at 12%/yr).

Marissa Cole
Head of Revenue Finance
Redwood Inference
Attachment: price-modeling-3yr-sensitivity.pdf

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai; ben_carter@redwood.ai; marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-12T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Executive approval: conditional 36-month price shelter for OptiMed

Team — after reviewing the ask, the modeling, and the proposed guardrails, I approve a conditional 36-month price shelter for OptiMed with the following executive-level constraints (to be inserted into the Master Agreement):

1) Uplift cap: Max 5% per 12-month period on the customer-facing rate, except for cost-pass events (e.g., new mandatory taxes or third-party cloud surcharge).
2) Consumption true-up: Quarterly reconciliation; if average monthly consumption >35% above forecast for two consecutive quarters, Redwood may initiate a 90-day repricing discussion limited to the incremental volume.
3) Discount limit: Aggregate discount not to exceed 18% over the term.
4) SLO remediation: Replace proposed 8% cash holdback with quarterly SLO credits up to 4% per quarter (max 12%/yr); credits apply to subsequent invoices.
5) Documentation & approvals: Legal to finalize renewal protection language with carve-outs; Revenue Finance to confirm final attachments and sign-off on the pricing schedule before signature.

Lauren — proceed to Legal for final contract edits and confirm OptiMed procurement deadline (2028-03-20). Ben/Marissa, escalate if any change to the constraints above.

-Markus
Chief Revenue Officer (acting)
Redwood Inference
